case_name: Messrs. Dwarka Prasad Laxmi Narain v State of Uttar Pradesh and Two Others
respondent: State of Uttar Pradesh and Two
facts: This is an application presented by the petitioners u/art. 32 of the Constitution, complaining of infraction of their fundamental rights guaranteed u/arts. 14 and cls. (f) and (g) of art. 19 (1) of the Constitution and praying for enforcement of the same by issue of writs in the nature of mandamus.
The petitioners are a firm of traders who had, prior to the cancellation of their licence, been carrying on the business of retail sellers of coal at a coal depot held by them in the town of Kanpur.

It is said that the District Magistrate of Kanpur as well as the District Supply Officer, who figure respectively as respondents Nos. 2 and 3 in the petition, had been for a considerable time past issuing directives from time to time upon the petitioners as well as other coal depot holders of the town, imposing restrictions of various kinds upon the sale of coal, soft coke, etc.

The landed costs comprised several items and besides ex-colliery price, the middleman's commission and the railway freight, there were incidental expenses of various kinds including labour duty, loading and unloading charges, cartage and stacking expenses.
On the 14th of February, 1953, the District Supply Officer issued a directive reducing the selling prices of coke, coal, etc., much below the existing rates.
There was an application for ad interim stay in connection with this petition which came up for hearing before the learned Vacation Judge of this court on the Ist of July, 1953.

The order of the 14th February was in fact withdrawn, but on the 10th of July, 1953, the State of Uttar Pradesh promulgated by a notification an order intituled 'The Uttar Pradesh Coal Control Order, 1953' purporting to act in exercise of the powers conferred upon it by s. 3(2) of the Essential Supplies Act, 1946, read with the notified order of the Government of India issued u/s. 4 of the Act.

The petitioners submitted an explanation which was not considered to be satisfactory and by an order dated the 13th of October, 1953, the District Supply Officer, Kanpur, cancelled the petitioners' licence.
issues: What is the validity of the Uttar Pradesh Coal Control Order, 1953?
Do the restrictions imposed by the order infringe on the fundamental rights of the petitioners under arts. 14 and 19 of the Constitution?
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners argued that the Uttar Pradesh Coal Control Order, 1953, is invalid as it infringes on their fundamental rights under arts. 14 and 19 of the Constitution.
The petitioners also argued that the order is arbitrary and unreasonable as it does not provide a fair margin of profit for coal traders.
The petitioners further argued that the order is violative of the principles of equality and non-discrimination as it treats all coal traders equally without regard to their individual circumstances.
respondent_arguments: The respondents argued that the Uttar Pradesh Coal Control Order, 1953, is valid as it is necessary for the control and regulation of the coal industry in the state.
The respondents also argued that the order is reasonable and fair as it provides a uniform price structure for all coal traders in the state.
The respondents further argued that the order does not infringe on the fundamental rights of the petitioners under arts. 14 and 19 of the Constitution.
court_reasoning: The court held that the Uttar Pradesh Coal Control Order, 1953, is invalid as it infringes on the fundamental rights of the petitioners under arts. 14 and 19 of the Constitution.
The court also held that the order is arbitrary and unreasonable as it does not provide a fair margin of profit for coal traders.
The court further held that the order is violative of the principles of equality and non-discrimination as it treats all coal traders equally without regard to their individual circumstances.
holding: The court declared the Uttar Pradesh Coal Control Order, 1953, invalid and unconstitutional.
The court also ordered the respondents to withdraw the order and not to enforce it against the petitioners or any other coal trader in the state.
